task_summary: Clarify the owner-observed difference between motor rotation and impeller rotation, and update the same fan-diagnosis round without more powered trials.

acceptance: Preserve original evidence and append the clarified physical observation.
Prioritize the mechanical interface while distinguishing stationary housing from the impeller.
Do not turn a user observation into proof of complete electrical health.
completed: Owner distinguished continuous motor rotation from absent impeller following.
Manufacturer assembly instructions and independent native review support inspecting attachment and part identification first.
Updated project handoff without changing firmware, parameters or hardware state.
remaining: Actual impeller attachment and component identification require power-off visual inspection.

metrics.name: continuation_interval
metrics.basis: First measured clock to cutoff; includes owner clarification and source review.

metrics.name: native_review_workers
metrics.basis: One bounded interpretation review; no hardware access.

observations: The initial phrase was ambiguous between rotor shudder, independent motor/impeller rotation and sound-only observation. One concise clarification materially changed diagnostic priority.
Old powered-trial evidence was retained rather than rewritten as an established electrical fault.

recommendations.action: Record which physical part is moving before using rotation or nonrotation as a diagnostic observation.
recommendations.next_check: Next inspection distinguishes impeller, rotor and stationary enclosure.

limits: No new electrical or physical measurement.
Exact installed motor and impeller attachment not visually verified.
No matched workflow baseline; efficiency improvement remains unproven.
